fields.Participants: Legal (links to VS-100), Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), CEO/CFO, affected business leads, external counsel
fields.Trigger: Maintained relationship; PCC inquiry/guidance; policy consultation

workflows.name: Philippine Competition Commission (PCC) Relationship & Engagement Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accountable point of contact, awareness of current PCC…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "VP Legal maintain the inquiry-response playbook and dawn-raid plan" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalate any PCC inquiry/investigation to the Board Audit/Risk Committee" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-619 (ensure controlled execution — Competition Authority (PCC) Engagement, Investigation & Remediation (PA-129.3).)
- operational: single accountable contact; operational: privilege protocol
Pain Points / Risks: - **Uncoordinated-response risk**: Multiple parties engaging PCC inconsistently; mitigated by single accountable contact
- **Privilege risk**: Sensitive advice not protected; mitigated by privilege protocol
System Touchpoints: - Legal matter mgmt (links to VS-100); govt affairs (links to VS-104); records/legal hold (links to VS-88); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: VP Legal own the PCC relationship: a single accountable point of contact, awareness of current PCC priorities/guidelines/enforcement trends, participation in PCC public consultations (links to VS-104), and engagement of qualified external competition counsel on retainer

VP Legal maintain the inquiry-response playbook and dawn-raid plan (links to W3970), the records/legal-hold interface (links to VS-88/W3970), and the privilege protocol for competition-sensitive advice
VP Legal/CEO escalate any PCC inquiry/investigation to the Board Audit/Risk Committee (links to VS-36) and activate matter management (links to VS-100)

fields.Participants: Legal, Compliance, IT (links to VS-27), Records (links to VS-88), Security (links to VS-23), affected site leadership, external counsel, executive team
fields.Trigger: PCC information request, summons, or unannounced inspection (dawn raid)

workflows.name: Competition Inquiry, Dawn Raid & Information Request Response

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "VP Legal execute the dawn-raid plan on unannounced inspection" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "log review, legal hold" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System continuous audit of "VP Legal debrief, preserve lessons, brief the Board Audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-619 (ensure controlled execution — Competition Authority (PCC) Engagement, Investigation & Remediation (PA-129.3).)
- operational: plan, training, and on-site leadership; operational: scope negotiation and log review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Obstruction risk**: Staff actions interpreted as obstruction; mitigated by plan, training, and on-site leadership
- **Over-production risk**: Privileged or out-of-scope material produced; mitigated by scope negotiation and log review
System Touchpoints: - Legal (links to VS-100); IT/records/legal-hold (links to VS-88/VS-27); security (links to VS-23); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: VP Legal execute the dawn-raid plan on unannounced inspection: verify PCC authority and scope, contact external counsel, manage staff conduct (courtesy, no obstruction, no destruction of documents), and document everything seized/requested
VP Legal manage information requests/summonses: scope negotiation, privilege/log review, legal hold (links to VS-88), controlled production, and tracking
VP Legal debrief, preserve lessons, brief the Board Audit Committee (links to VS-36), and adjust controls/training (links to W3960/W3968)

fields.Participants: Legal, external competition counsel, affected business unit, Compliance (links to VS-119), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), CEO
fields.Trigger: PCC preliminary inquiry, formal investigation, or motu proprio (own-motion) case

workflows.name: PCC Investigation, Preliminary Inquiry & Motu Proprio Matter Defense

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document review, data analytics" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "VP Legal manage the matter lifecycle" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "prepare for PCC adjudication and any subsequent appeal" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-619 (ensure controlled execution — Competition Authority (PCC) Engagement, Investigation & Remediation (PA-129.3).)
- operational: external counsel and analytics; operational: communications plan (links to VS-14)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Weak-defense risk**: Inadequate factual/legal analysis; mitigated by external counsel and analytics
- **Reputational risk**: Investigation becoming public; mitigated by communications plan (links to VS-14.3)
System Touchpoints: - Legal matter mgmt (links to VS-100); records (links to VS-88); analytics (links to VS-28); governance (links to VS-36); ethics (links to VS-119)

steps.activity: VP Legal/external-counsel conduct the matter defense: factual investigation (internal interviews, document review, data analytics), legal analysis (no-infringement / no-effect / exemption defenses), and response to the Statement of Objections / PCC preliminary determination

VP Legal manage the matter lifecycle: evidence and privilege management (links to VS-88), internal communications controls, board reporting (links to VS-36), and decision on leniency/settlement vs full defense (links to W3972)
VP Legal prepare for PCC adjudication and any subsequent appeal (links to W3973); coordinate settlement/commitment options (links to W3972) and disclosure (links to W3974)

fields.Participants: VP Legal, external competition counsel, CEO, Board Audit Committee, Compliance (links to VS-119), affected executives/staff
fields.Trigger: Detected cartel/serious conduct; PCC offer of settlement/commitment; strategic leniency application

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "file a leniency/marker application with the PCC for immunity/reduced fines,…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "VP Legal execute the chosen path" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-619 (ensure controlled execution — Competition Authority (PCC) Engagement, Investigation & Remediation (PA-129.3).)
- operational: rapid assessment on detection; operational: careful scoping
Pain Points / Risks: - **Missed-leniency risk**: Late application loses immunity; mitigated by rapid assessment on detection
- **Over-admission risk**: Settlement admissions widen private-action exposure; mitigated by careful scoping
System Touchpoints: - Legal (links to VS-100); ethics/speak-up (links to VS-119); records (links to VS-88); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: VP Legal/external-counsel assess leniency/marker eligibility for any detected cartel conduct (price-fixing, bid-rigging, market/customer allocation) and decide whether to file a leniency/marker application with the PCC for immunity/reduced fines, coordinating with speak-up (links to VS-119)
VP Legal assess settlement vs full-defense vs commitment options during a PCC matter, weighing fine reduction, conduct-change obligations, admission scope, and downstream private-action exposure
VP Legal execute the chosen path (leniency cooperation, settlement agreement, or binding commitments), manage the obligations, and document the decision basis (links to records VS-88)

fields.Participants: VP Legal, external litigation counsel, CEO, Board, affected executives, Finance (links to VS-17.4), Records (links to VS-88)
fields.Trigger: PCC decision; private competition damages suit; appeal

workflows.name: Competition Litigation, Appeal (Court of Appeals / SC) & Judgment Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-record of "record preparation, briefs, and oral argument" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate with insurance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document lessons and update controls" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-619 (ensure controlled execution — Competition Authority (PCC) Engagement, Investigation & Remediation (PA-129.3).)
- operational: strong appellate counsel; operational: early scoping and reserves (links to VS-17)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Adverse-precedent risk**: Loss creates binding precedent; mitigated by strong appellate counsel
- **Damages-exposure risk**: Private actions following enforcement; mitigated by early scoping and reserves (links to VS-17.4)
System Touchpoints: - Legal/litigation (links to VS-100); records (links to VS-88); insurance (links to VS-26); finance (links to VS-17.4)

steps.activity: VP Legal/external-counsel manage the appeal of any adverse PCC decision to the Court of Appeals and, if warranted, the Supreme Court, including record preparation, briefs, and oral argument
VP Legal/external-counsel defend private competition damages actions (follow-on or standalone), manage discovery/class-style claims exposure, and coordinate with insurance (links to VS-26)
VP Legal manage judgment, settlement, and enforcement; document lessons and update controls (links to W3975)

fields.Participants: Finance (links to VS-17.4), Treasury (links to VS-18), Legal (links to VS-100), Tax (links to VS-79), Corporate Communications (links to VS-14.3), Investor/debt-holder relations
fields.Trigger: PCC fine/penalty imposed; damages award/settlement; disclosure obligation

workflows.name: Competition Penalty, Fine & Damages Payment & Disclosure Management

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow orchestration of "coordinate any insurance recovery" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-619 (ensure controlled execution — Competition Authority (PCC) Engagement, Investigation & Remediation (PA-129.3).)
- operational: PAS 37 provisioning and external counsel estimate; operational: disclosure protocol and covenant review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-provision risk**: Fine/contingency mis-stated; mitigated by PAS 37 provisioning and external counsel estimate
- **Disclosure-timing risk**: Late/mis-timed disclosure; mitigated by disclosure protocol and covenant review
System Touchpoints: - Finance (links to VS-17.4); treasury (links to VS-18); tax (links to VS-79); legal (links to VS-100); comms (links to VS-14.3); insurance (links to VS-26)

steps.activity: CFO/Legal quantify and provide for any PCC fine/penalty (up to PHP 250M first offense for a corporate offender; substantially more for repeat/large offenders under RA 10667) and any damages award/settlement; book the provision and contingency (links to VS-17.4 PFRS PAS 37)
Treasury/Finance manage payment within PCC/deadline, assess fine tax-deductibility (links to VS-79), and coordinate any insurance recovery (links to VS-26)

Legal/Comms manage disclosure (to the Board, debt-holders/lenders per covenants, and any required public/regulatory disclosure), communications (links to VS-14.3), and reputation management (links to VS-104)

fields.Participants: Legal, Compliance, affected business unit, Internal Audit (links to VS-21), Procurement (links to VS-03), Merchandising (links to VS-01), external monitor (if appointed)
fields.Trigger: PCC commitment/order; settlement obligation; post-incident corrective action

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitor appointed by the PCC, and report progress to the Board Audit Committee" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "verify remediation effectiveness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-619 (ensure controlled execution — Competition Authority (PCC) Engagement, Investigation & Remediation (PA-129.3).)
- operational: monitoring and tracking; operational: clear terms and cooperation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-compliance-with-commitment risk**: Breach of commitment/order triggers further enforcement; mitigated by monitoring and tracking
- **Monitor-conflict risk**: External monitor scope disputes; mitigated by clear terms and cooperation
System Touchpoints: - Legal (links to VS-100); audit (links to VS-21); procurement (links to VS-03); merchandising (links to VS-01); records (links to VS-88); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: VP Legal translate any PCC commitment/order, settlement obligation, or conduct-change remedy into a remediation plan: clause amendments, conduct changes, training (links to W3960), control changes (W3961–W3966), and structural/divestiture remedies if imposed
VP Legal/Compliance implement the plan, support any external compliance monitor appointed by the PCC, and report progress to the Board Audit Committee (links to VS-36)
Internal Audit/Legal verify remediation effectiveness (links to VS-21), close the matter, and embed lessons into the program (W3968/W3976)

fields.Participants: Legal, Compliance, Data/Analytics (links to VS-28), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), CEO, Board Audit/Risk Committee
fields.Trigger: Board/Audit Committee cadence; annual program review

workflows.name: Competition Compliance Program Analytics, Reporting & Board Oversight

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews completed, monitoring anomalies, PCC engagements, incidents,…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "report to the Board Audit/Risk Committee" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-619 (ensure controlled execution — Competition Authority (PCC) Engagement, Investigation & Remediation (PA-129.3).)
- operational: structured quarterly reporting; operational: annual review and benchmarking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Board-blind-spot risk**: Competition exposure under-reported to the Board; mitigated by structured quarterly reporting
- **Maturity-stagnation risk**: Program not improving; mitigated by annual review and benchmarking
System Touchpoints: - Analytics (links to VS-28); audit/ERM (links to VS-21); governance (links to VS-36); strategy (links to VS-33); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: VP Legal/Analytics compile program analytics: risk-coverage %, training completion, control-testing pass rate, association-meeting reports filed, contract-clause reviews completed, monitoring anomalies, PCC engagements, incidents, remediation status, and KPI trends

VP Legal report to the Board Audit/Risk Committee (links to VS-36 governance and VS-21.2 ERM), flag emerging risks (PCC guidance, market changes, M&A pipeline links to VS-130), and seek direction on risk appetite
VP Legal run the annual program review (effectiveness, resourcing, maturity benchmarking against PCC/ISO 37001-style expectations), secure budget, and iterate the strategy (links to W3953)
